disputed: DHS and the administration deny any white-nationalist intent behind specific imagery choices, characterizing them as ordinary recruitment and security messaging. Whether the seal redesign and 'at war' framing reflects a genuine operational posture versus rhetorical escalation is a matter of interpretation; Mullin's own framing acknowledges it is intended as a symbolic statement about posture, not a description of a new legal or military status.

items: In September 2026, ahead of the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced the department's seal will be redesigned so its eagle faces arrows rather than an olive branch/palm - Mullin said the palm 'represents peace,' while facing the arrows 'signals war,' and described DHS as an agency 'at war every single day' against terrorists, cartels, and cyberattackers. No effective date or official document detailing the redesign had been provided as of the report. (The Dregs Report, citing Fox News (https://thedregsreport.com/2026/09/08/dhs-seal-will-face-arrows-as-markwayne-mullin-cites-changing-daily-threats/))
sections.label: Seal redesign

items: DHS has repeatedly posted content using World War II-era propaganda imagery, including an 'Uncle Sam' poster urging people to 'report all foreign invaders' to ICE, and a 1943 U.S. Capitol image captioned 'We Can Return,' posted after Trump said he would rid Washington, DC of 'Crime, Savagery, Filth, and Scum.' (Yahoo/AP (https://www.yahoo.com/news/dhs-sends-provocative-poster-143430525.html); CNN (https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/13/politics/homeland-security-department-social-media))

In January 2026, DHS posted an ICE recruitment ad captioned 'WE'LL HAVE OUR HOME AGAIN,' a phrase from a song popularized by white nationalist groups including the Proud Boys; then-DHS spokeswoman Tricia McLaughlin denied any such connection. The post drew wide press coverage and was later removed. The Global Project Against Hate and Extremism reported similar imagery resumed after Mullin's appointment as DHS Secretary in mid-March 2026. (Global Project Against Hate and Extremism (https://globalextremism.org/post/dhs-continues-to-post-white-supremacist-and-christian-nationalist-content/))

A UC Berkeley public law professor, Ian Haney Lopez, described DHS's 'heritage'/'homeland' messaging as 'an active effort to promote lies designed to create fear and hysteria,' saying it was most reminiscent of 'demagogic eras' in other countries rather than prior U.S. propaganda efforts. The Southern Poverty Law Center's Hatewatch project quoted a social-justice group director saying the posts are 'not only intended to recruit staff but to normalize the dehumanization of immigrants.' (CNN (https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/13/politics/homeland-security-department-social-media); SPLC (https://www.splcenter.org/resources/hatewatch/dhs-white-nationalist-anti-immigrant-social-media/))
